requirement: v3.5.8 release candidate: prove the Teams WebRTC data plane sends an artifact end to end across four machines in both directions, returns only after the receiver acknowledges SHA-256 + sink completion, and never falls back to Relay when the 33-attempt budget is exhausted.

assertions.matrix: 12 of 12 directed legs passed across CloudHost, MacMini, IM2A and HSD: 1 MiB legs used 6 chunks/attempts and 256 KiB legs used 2; every sender returned ok:true with send.ack.ok:true, and every receiver reported artifact-received with a sink file whose SHA-256 and byte count match the sender's artifact.
assertions.ack: ACK was emitted only after the receiver reassembled the chunks, verified SHA-256 and wrote the sink; ACK frames are separate from the 33-attempt chunk budget.
assertions.negative_33: With no receiver and a short connect window, sendArtifact returned TEAM_DATA_P2P_EXHAUSTED after exactly 33 attempts in 41.283 s; the alert says the relay was not used, and peerStatus reported WEBRTC_CONNECT_TIMEOUT instead of null.
assertions.relay_ledger: The deliver phase was driven with a WebRTC result path that failed 33 times; it still called POST /v1/result exactly once and delivered the envelope.
assertions.node_test: node --test test/relay-ledger.test.mjs test/peer-status-last-error.test.mjs: 2 tests, 2 pass, 0 fail.
assertions.receiver_fallback: A receiver path recorded as fallback_after_receive means the artifact had already passed SHA-256 and been written to the sink before the transport closed; it is not a data-plane failure.
assertions.scope: TOFUTURE was offline during this run and is excluded from the four-node matrix; its code copy was not re-measured in this round.
